title: elitea.audit.v1 evidence event
description: One audit evidence event, as exported to a SIEM by the OTLP logs and signed webhook exporters (ADR-0042 decision 3). Producers: services/elitea-main/internal/auditexport maps securityaudit records and centry.audit_events rows to this envelope. OCSF mapping (https://schema.ocsf.io): event_id -> metadata.uid; time -> time; source -> metadata.product.feature.name; ocsf.class_uid / ocsf.category_uid -> class_uid / category_uid; tenant.project_id -> cloud.project_uid; actor.id -> actor.user.uid (actor.type decides user, service or agent); actor.email -> actor.user.email_addr; action -> activity_name; target.type / target.id / target.name -> resources[].type / uid / name; outcome -> status_id (success, failure) and authorization disposition (allow, deny); correlation.trace_id -> metadata.correlation_uid; details.http_method / http_route / status_code -> http_request.http_method / url.path / http_response.code. chain.* and details.* have no OCSF attribute and travel in unmapped. A field is omitted, never null, when it has no value, except tenant.project_id which is null for platform-wide events. Adding an optional field is not a version change; renaming, removing or retyping one, or adding a required one, is a new schema version.

schema.description: The schema version. A consumer rejects or quarantines a version it does not know.

event_id.description: Stable identifier of the event. Delivery is at least once, so a consumer deduplicates on it. A security audit event keeps its CloudEvents UUID; an audit_events row has a name-based UUID derived from its row id.

time.description: When the audited operation happened (UTC, RFC 3339).

source.description: Which evidence stream produced the event. security_audit is the governed security audit outbox; admin_audit is centry.audit_events (the HTTP access audit behind the admin Audit Trail). run_step, approval and suspension are reserved for ADR-0042 evidence added later.

event_type.description: The producer's event type: a CloudEvents type such as ai.elitea.security.v1.decision for security_audit, or the audit_events event_type (api, socketio, rpc, agent, tool, llm, schedule, admin_task) for admin_audit.

ocsf.description: The OCSF class when one fits (3003 Authorize Session, 3004 Entity Management, 3005 User Access Management, 6003 API Activity). Omitted when no class fits.

project_id.description: The tenant project. 0 is the platform partition of the security audit chain; null means the row carries no project.

id.description: A user id, a principal reference or an agent identity reference. "unknown" when the producer recorded none.

chain.description: The RFC 8693 actor chain, outermost first, as references.

fidelity.description: How faithfully the actor chain was established (ADR-0039 decision 5).

action.description: The governed operation (credential.use, grant.revoke) or, for admin_audit, the label "METHOD /route".

target.description: What the action acted on, when the producer recorded it.

outcome.description: allow and deny are authorisation decisions; success and failure are the result of an operation.

partition.description: The hash chain partition (the tenant project id; 0 is the platform).

sequence.description: Position in the partition chain: 1, 2, 3 with no gap.

prev_hash.description: Hex SHA-256 of the previous event; 64 zeros for the first event of a partition.

hash.description: Hex SHA-256 over prev_hash and the canonical stored event. Verify with the elitea-main security audit verifier; the hash covers the stored CloudEvents form, not this envelope.

chain.description: Present when the producer keeps a tamper-evident chain (security_audit today).

details.description: Source-specific fields. The shape is fixed per source; run_step, approval and suspension add theirs later.

outbox_seq.description: The global outbox sequence, for tracing a record to its row.

http_route.description: The matched route pattern, never the raw target.
